status: Fixed before calculating the new OOB-selector results; original cohort outcomes and previous comparison results were already known
authorization: New advisor request for additional comparisons and a practical method-selection recommendation
question: Can calibration-only resampling select whether and how much to update more reliably than fixed updating strategies?
scope: One established selection framework adapted to censored outcomes; no new predictor training, no revival or threshold search for the rejected event-gated rules
source: Davis et al. 2019, doi:10.1093/jamia/ocz127; original two-stage pooled OOB-record bootstrap, adapted to IPCW and this three-method candidate set
outer_allocations: Original sorted-patient permutations, seed+100000*cohort_index+repeat; main calibration prefixes; original remaining and common suffix evaluations unchanged
inner_pairing: SeedSequence([inner_seed,cohort_index,outer_repeat]); identical bootstrap patient indices and second-stage pool indices across the three predictors
candidate_order_rationale: Predefined preference for no fitted update, then shrinkage toward zero, then unrestricted intercept; penalized and ordinary intercept both have one coefficient, so order expresses preference rather than a new parameter count
stage1: Draw n_cal patients with replacement B1 times. Fit each update on in-bag records, with in-bag KM censoring weights re-estimated. Predict only patients absent from that bootstrap. Pool all OOB patient-replicate records, retaining repeated predictions for the same patient; do not average probabilities before scoring.
selection_weights: Estimate G on the entire calibration sample, then attach its horizon IPCW outcome/weight to every pooled OOB record of each patient. This scoring nuisance estimate uses only calibration outcomes and never enters an OOB prediction. It is an explicit censored-outcome adaptation of the binary-outcome reference.
stage2: Draw n_cal paired records from the pooled OOB set B2 times. For each candidate, calculate sum(w*(y-q)^2)/n_cal. Identify the candidate with lowest median resampled Brier score (ties follow candidate order).
OOB_min: Select the lowest-median candidate; diagnostic comparator using exactly the same resamples as the primary selector
OOB_simple: Primary selector: compare candidates preceding OOB_min in the fixed order. Choose the first whose paired Brier-difference percentile interval [2.5%,97.5%] contains zero; otherwise retain OOB_min. This is an operational adaptation, not a claim of validated nominal coverage in sparse censored samples.
final_fit: Apply the selected method refitted on all calibration patients; use archived full-calibration coefficients where available and verify replay. Evaluation outcomes are accessed only after selection.
boundaries: Retain zero-event and all-event bootstrap draws: ordinary gives constant zero/one; kappa5 is finite. If no horizon outcomes are observable, all update predictions revert to unchanged and the case is recorded. Do not omit or redraw difficult bootstrap samples. Record OOB coverage.
evaluation: Primary original remaining-patient IPCW Brier, with actual evaluation-subset censoring weights. Common suffix sensitivity reuses identical selected coefficients. No evaluation information enters selection.
reporting: mean Brier for each cohort and predictor
90th percentile of loss relative to unchanged
interpretation: Repeated allocations describe this fixed data setting. Selection is calibration-only but the cohorts remain exploratory because historical results motivated the study. A practical recommendation must reflect cohort/predictor exceptions and must not convert retrospective cohort winners into a new deployable threshold.
numerical_checks: Independent recomputation of selected methods from saved inner summaries
continuation: First ten outer repeats per cohort validate implementation and runtime only; no efficacy-based pruning or tuning of this published-comparator experiment. Then complete all300 if numerical checks pass. If unexpectedly expensive, report measured runtime before a recorded implementation-only adjustment.
stop: Finish this fixed main-budget comparison and summarize a method-selection recommendation. Do not add new models, penalties, thresholds, alpha values, resampling schemes, or seeds to rescue results. The earlier event-selector pilot remains stopped.
